Alright, the recent edits to `src/commands.ts` have been type‑checked and the project builds without errors. I added the cost field to the `runCommand` signature, imported `formatCost`, and updated the usage output to display the computed cost. The keybindings help text was also expanded. After running `bunx tsc` everything passed, and the `bun build` succeeded, producing a new binary at `dist/glint`.

The next step is to replace the existing installed binary (`~/.local/bin/glint`) with this freshly built version and then verify that the changes are reflected when the CLI runs. However, when I first tried to copy the binary, the system complained that the target file was “Text file busy”. That indicates that some process still has the old binary open—most likely a lingering `glint` process from a previous tmux session.

I already attempted to kill the tmux session (`tmux kill-session -t glint`) and even used `pkill -f "local/bin/glint"` but the file remained busy. To get to the root of it, I listed the processes holding the file with `fuser` and saw two PIDs (563021 and 588034). I then explicitly killed those PIDs (`kill 563021 588034`) and confirmed the copy succeeded (`COPIED`). At this point the new binary is safely in place.

Now I need to actually run the updated binary to see the new intro output, especially the cost line I added. The most reliable way to capture the TUI output without interfering with my current terminal is to launch `glint` inside a detached tmux session, let it render for a short moment, then capture the pane contents. I’ll use the same dimensions (`-x 110 -y 36`) and working directory (`/tmp/glint-test`) that I’ve been using for earlier captures, and redirect any error output to a temporary log file (`/tmp/glint-tui-err.log`) so it doesn’t pollute the pane.

I need to give the process enough time to draw the introductory UI before I snapshot it. Previously I used `sleep 1.1` or `sleep 1.2`; a slightly shorter pause (`0.9` s) should still be sufficient while keeping the test fast. To make sure I see the full multi‑line intro—including the new cost line—I’ll capture more lines than before; `head -25` should comfortably include the entire header.

Putting this together, the command sequence will be:
1. `tmux new-session -d -s glint -x 110 -y 36 -c /tmp/glint-test 'glint 2>/tmp/glint-tui-err.log'` – start the binary in a detached session.
2. `sleep 0.9` – wait for the UI to render.
3. `tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\\s*$' | head -25` – grab the pane output, strip blank lines, and show the first 25 lines.

This will let me verify that the updated usage display (including the cost) appears correctly in the CLI’s intro. Hence I’ll issue this exact Bash tool call.
